model_attempts.prompt:
# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 1 / 30
Penalty so far for 0 wrong guesses: 0
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 30

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥

#### Your hand

10♣, 2♠, 3♣, 10♣, 8♦, 10♥, J♥, 2♥, 9♣, 9♥, 5♥, 7♣

#### Your recent play history



#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "One sentence summary of your analysis and why you're playing this card",
    "card": "5♥" (the card symbol from your hand, must be the exact symbol e.g., "5♥", "K♠", "A♦",...)
    "tentative_rule": "Your current best guess about the rule",
    "confidence_level": 0-10,
    "guess_rule": true or false (whether to officially try to guess the rule this turn)
}
</ACTION>

Always provide your current best hypothesis as a tentative rule, even if you're uncertain.
If you set guess_rule to false, this tentative rule will not be evaluated, it's just for your own tracking.
Set "guess_rule" to true only when you want to officially try to guess the rule.
   - If correct, you score and the round ends immediately.
   - If incorrect, you will lose 2 points from your final score, and the round continues.

#### Example:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "I see red and black cards alternating. My 3♥ is red, last card was black.",
    "card": "3♥",
    "tentative_rule": "Cards must alternate between red and black colors",
    "confidence_level": 8,
    "guess_rule": false
}
</ACTION>

# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 2 / 30
Penalty so far for 0 wrong guesses: 0
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 29

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠]

#### Your hand

10♣, 3♣, 10♣, 8♦, 10♥, J♥, 2♥, 9♣, 9♥, 5♥, 7♣, 6♣

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- 2♠: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: With only A♥ accepted so far, I'm testing whether color matters by playing a black spade; rejection would support a red/heart rule, while acceptance would suggest alternation or another property.


#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "One sentence summary of your analysis and why you're playing this card",
    "card": "5♥" (the card symbol from your hand, must be the exact symbol e.g., "5♥", "K♠", "A♦",...)
    "tentative_rule": "Your current best guess about the rule",
    "confidence_level": 0-10,
    "guess_rule": true or false (whether to officially try to guess the rule this turn)
}
</ACTION>

Always provide your current best hypothesis as a tentative rule, even if you're uncertain.
If you set guess_rule to false, this tentative rule will not be evaluated, it's just for your own tracking.
Set "guess_rule" to true only when you want to officially try to guess the rule.
   - If correct, you score and the round ends immediately.
   - If incorrect, you will lose 2 points from your final score, and the round continues.

    "confidence_level": 8,
    "guess_rule": false
}
</ACTION>

model_attempts.prompt:
# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 3 / 30
Penalty so far for 0 wrong guesses: 0
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 28

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣]

#### Your hand

10♣, 10♣, 8♦, 10♥, J♥, 2♥, 9♣, 9♥, 5♥, 7♣, 6♣, 4♦

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- 2♠: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: With only A♥ accepted so far, I'm testing whether color matters by playing a black spade; rejection would support a red/heart rule, while acceptance would suggest alternation or another property.
- 3♣: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: Only one accepted red heart and one rejected black spade, so I'll play 3♣ (black odd) to test whether rejection is due to color/black or to rank parity/other properties—if it is accepted, color/heart rules are ruled out.


#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "One sentence summary of your analysis and why you're playing this card",
    "card": "5♥" (the card symbol from your hand, must be the exact symbol e.g., "5♥", "K♠", "A♦",...)
    "tentative_rule": "Your current best guess about the rule",
    "confidence_level": 0-10,
    "guess_rule": true or false (whether to officially try to guess the rule this turn)
}
</ACTION>

Always provide your current best hypothesis as a tentative rule, even if you're uncertain.
If you set guess_rule to false, this tentative rule will not be evaluated, it's just for your own tracking.
Set "guess_rule" to true only when you want to officially try to guess the rule.
   - If correct, you score and the round ends immediately.
   - If incorrect, you will lose 2 points from your final score, and the round continues.

#### Example:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "I see red and black cards alternating. My 3♥ is red, last card was black.",
    "card": "3♥",
    "tentative_rule": "Cards must alternate between red and black colors",
    "confidence_level": 8,
    "guess_rule": false
}
</ACTION>

# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:

model_attempts.prompt:
# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 5 / 30
Penalty so far for 0 wrong guesses: 0
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 26

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣] [8♦] [10♥]

#### Your hand

10♣, 10♣, J♥, 2♥, 9♣, 9♥, 5♥, 7♣, 6♣, 4♦, 3♣, Q♣

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- 3♣: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: Only one accepted red heart and one rejected black spade, so I'll play 3♣ (black odd) to test whether rejection is due to color/black or to rank parity/other properties—if it is accepted, color/heart rules are ruled out.
- 8♦: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: Only A♥ has been accepted and both black cards rejected, so I need to test whether a red non-heart (diamond) is accepted to distinguish a red-color rule from a hearts-only rule.
- 10♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejected cards so far are non-hearts, but I haven't tested a heart yet, so I'll play 10♥ (an even heart) to distinguish 'hearts only' from rules like 'red odd'.


#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:

}

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 6 / 30
Penalty so far for 0 wrong guesses: 0
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 25

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣] [8♦] [10♥] [J♥]

#### Your hand

10♣, 10♣, 2♥, 9♣, 9♥, 5♥, 7♣, 6♣, 4♦, 3♣, Q♣, 5♣

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- 8♦: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: Only A♥ has been accepted and both black cards rejected, so I need to test whether a red non-heart (diamond) is accepted to distinguish a red-color rule from a hearts-only rule.
- 10♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejected cards so far are non-hearts, but I haven't tested a heart yet, so I'll play 10♥ (an even heart) to distinguish 'hearts only' from rules like 'red odd'.
- J♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejected cards fail either the color or parity of the starter A♥, so I need to test a red odd card; J♥ is red and odd and also checks whether face cards are allowed.


#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "One sentence summary of your analysis and why you're playing this card",
    "card": "5♥" (the card symbol from your hand, must be the exact symbol e.g., "5♥", "K♠", "A♦",...)
    "tentative_rule": "Your current best guess about the rule",
    "confidence_level": 0-10,
    "guess_rule": true or false (whether to officially try to guess the rule this turn)
}
</ACTION>

Always provide your current best hypothesis as a tentative rule, even if you're uncertain.
If you set guess_rule to false, this tentative rule will not be evaluated, it's just for your own tracking.
Set "guess_rule" to true only when you want to officially try to guess the rule.
   - If correct, you score and the round ends immediately.
   - If incorrect, you will lose 2 points from your final score, and the round continues.

#### Example:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "I see red and black cards alternating. My 3♥ is red, last card was black.",
    "card": "3♥",
    "tentative_rule": "Cards must alternate between red and black colors",
    "confidence_level": 8,
    "guess_rule": false
}
</ACTION>

model_attempts.prompt:
# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 7 / 30
Penalty so far for 1 wrong guesses: 2
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 22

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣] [8♦] [10♥] [J♥] [9♥]

#### Your hand

10♣, 10♣, 2♥, 9♣, 5♥, 7♣, 6♣, 4♦, 3♣, Q♣, 5♣, 3♦

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- 10♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejected cards so far are non-hearts, but I haven't tested a heart yet, so I'll play 10♥ (an even heart) to distinguish 'hearts only' from rules like 'red odd'.
- J♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejected cards fail either the color or parity of the starter A♥, so I need to test a red odd card; J♥ is red and odd and also checks whether face cards are allowed.
- 9♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejections so far are either black, even, or a face card, so the remaining untested category is a red odd non-face; I'll play 9♥ to test and guess that rule.


#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)

- "Cards must be red, have an odd rank, and not be a face card."

All these guesses were incorrect.


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "One sentence summary of your analysis and why you're playing this card",
    "card": "5♥" (the card symbol from your hand, must be the exact symbol e.g., "5♥", "K♠", "A♦",...)
    "tentative_rule": "Your current best guess about the rule",
    "confidence_level": 0-10,
    "guess_rule": true or false (whether to officially try to guess the rule this turn)
}
</ACTION>

Always provide your current best hypothesis as a tentative rule, even if you're uncertain.
If you set guess_rule to false, this tentative rule will not be evaluated, it's just for your own tracking.
Set "guess_rule" to true only when you want to officially try to guess the rule.
   - If correct, you score and the round ends immediately.
   - If incorrect, you will lose 2 points from your final score, and the round continues.

#### Example:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "I see red and black cards alternating. My 3♥ is red, last card was black.",
    "card": "3♥",
    "tentative_rule": "Cards must alternate between red and black colors",
    "confidence_level": 8,
    "guess_rule": false
}
</ACTION>

# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 8 / 30

Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 21

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣] [8♦] [10♥] [J♥] [9♥] 2♥

#### Your hand

10♣, 10♣, 9♣, 5♥, 7♣, 6♣, 4♦, 3♣, Q♣, 5♣, 3♦, J♦

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- J♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejected cards fail either the color or parity of the starter A♥, so I need to test a red odd card; J♥ is red and odd and also checks whether face cards are allowed.
- 9♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejections so far are either black, even, or a face card, so the remaining untested category is a red odd non-face; I'll play 9♥ to test and guess that rule.
- 2♥: ✓ ACCEPTED

model_attempts.prompt:
# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 9 / 30
Penalty so far for 1 wrong guesses: 2
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 20

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣] [8♦] [10♥] [J♥] [9♥] 2♥ 3♦

#### Your hand

10♣, 10♣, 9♣, 5♥, 7♣, 6♣, 4♦, 3♣, Q♣, 5♣, J♦, 6♣

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- 9♥: ✗ REJECTED
  Your reasoning: All rejections so far are either black, even, or a face card, so the remaining untested category is a red odd non-face; I'll play 9♥ to test and guess that rule.
- 2♥: ✓ ACCEPTED
  Your reasoning: All six rejected cards have rank greater than 1, so the simplest rule is that only Aces (rank 1) are accepted; I'm playing 2♥ as a low-heart check to rule out any same-suit/low-rank alternative before making another official guess.
- 3♦: ✓ ACCEPTED
  Your reasoning: The accepted cards A♥ and 2♥ suggest a rank-progression rule; playing 3♦ will tell whether the next card must share only the color (accept) or also the suit (reject) with the current last card 2♥.


#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)

- "Cards must be red, have an odd rank, and not be a face card."

All these guesses were incorrect.


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "One sentence summary of your analysis and why you're playing this card",
    "card": "5♥" (the card symbol from your hand, must be the exact symbol e.g., "5♥", "K♠", "A♦",...)
    "tentative_rule": "Your current best guess about the rule",
    "confidence_level": 0-10,
    "guess_rule": true or false (whether to officially try to guess the rule this turn)
}
</ACTION>

Always provide your current best hypothesis as a tentative rule, even if you're uncertain.
If you set guess_rule to false, this tentative rule will not be evaluated, it's just for your own tracking.
Set "guess_rule" to true only when you want to officially try to guess the rule.
   - If correct, you score and the round ends immediately.
   - If incorrect, you will lose 2 points from your final score, and the round continues.

    "tentative_rule": "Cards must alternate between red and black colors",
    "confidence_level": 8,
    "guess_rule": false
}
</ACTION>

# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 10 / 30
Penalty so far for 2 wrong guesses: 4
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 17

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣] [8♦] [10♥] [J♥] [9♥] 2♥ 3♦ 4♦

#### Your hand

10♣, 10♣, 9♣, 5♥, 7♣, 6♣, 3♣, Q♣, 5♣, J♦, 6♣, 6♥

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- 2♥: ✓ ACCEPTED
  Your reasoning: All six rejected cards have rank greater than 1, so the simplest rule is that only Aces (rank 1) are accepted; I'm playing 2♥ as a low-heart check to rule out any same-suit/low-rank alternative before making another official guess.
- 3♦: ✓ ACCEPTED
  Your reasoning: The accepted cards A♥ and 2♥ suggest a rank-progression rule; playing 3♦ will tell whether the next card must share only the color (accept) or also the suit (reject) with the current last card 2♥.
- 4♦: ✓ ACCEPTED
  Your reasoning: The accepted cards are all red and one rank higher than the previous mainline card, while every rejection fails either the color or the rank condition; I'm playing 4♦ as the required red next-rank card and guessing the rule now.


#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)

- "Cards must be red, have an odd rank, and not be a face card."
- "The card must be the same color as the last mainline card and have a rank exactly one higher than that card."

All these guesses were incorrect.


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "One sentence summary of your analysis and why you're playing this card",
    "card": "5♥" (the card symbol from your hand, must be the exact symbol e.g., "5♥", "K♠", "A♦",...)
    "tentative_rule": "Your current best guess about the rule",
    "confidence_level": 0-10,
    "guess_rule": true or false (whether to officially try to guess the rule this turn)
}
</ACTION>

Always provide your current best hypothesis as a tentative rule, even if you're uncertain.
If you set guess_rule to false, this tentative rule will not be evaluated, it's just for your own tracking.
Set "guess_rule" to true only when you want to officially try to guess the rule.
   - If correct, you score and the round ends immediately.
   - If incorrect, you will lose 2 points from your final score, and the round continues.

#### Example:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "I see red and black cards alternating. My 3♥ is red, last card was black.",
    "card": "3♥",
    "tentative_rule": "Cards must alternate between red and black colors",
    "confidence_level": 8,
    "guess_rule": false
}
</ACTION>

model_attempts.prompt:
# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 11 / 30
Penalty so far for 3 wrong guesses: 6
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 14

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣] [8♦] [10♥] [J♥] [9♥] 2♥ 3♦ 4♦ 5♥

#### Your hand

10♣, 10♣, 9♣, 7♣, 6♣, 3♣, Q♣, 5♣, J♦, 6♣, 6♥, J♣

#### Your recent play history

Your last 3 turns (the card you played, the outcome and your reasoning summary):
- 3♦: ✓ ACCEPTED
  Your reasoning: The accepted cards A♥ and 2♥ suggest a rank-progression rule; playing 3♦ will tell whether the next card must share only the color (accept) or also the suit (reject) with the current last card 2♥.
- 4♦: ✓ ACCEPTED
  Your reasoning: The accepted cards are all red and one rank higher than the previous mainline card, while every rejection fails either the color or the rank condition; I'm playing 4♦ as the required red next-rank card and guessing the rule now.
- 5♥: ✓ ACCEPTED
  Your reasoning: The accepted cards are all red and exactly one rank higher than the previous mainline card, so after 4♦ the needed red next-rank card is 5♥; the earlier 'same color' guess was too broad because the rule requires red, not merely matching the last card's color.


#### All your previous failed rule guesses (if any)

- "Cards must be red, have an odd rank, and not be a face card."
- "The card must be the same color as the last mainline card and have a rank exactly one higher than that card."
- "The card must be red and have a rank exactly one higher than the last mainline card."

All these guesses were incorrect.


### Task description and formatting instructions

You must select a card from your hand to play and optionally decide to try to guess the rule.

You will be asked to provide the following in your response:
- A short one sentence summary of your reasoning, explaining your thought process about the pattern so far and why you are playing the selected card.
- The card you are playing from your hand (must be one of the cards listed in your hand).
- Your current best guess about the hidden rule (must be clear and unequivocal).
- Your confidence level in your tentative guess rule on a scale of 0-10 (for instance 7 means "70% confident : there 70% probability to be correct")
- Whether you want to officially guess the rule this turn (true or false). Only set to true if you want to make an official guess with your tentative rule. Otherwise, your tentative rule is just for your own tracking and will not be evaluated this turn.

Format your response as follows:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "One sentence summary of your analysis and why you're playing this card",
    "card": "5♥" (the card symbol from your hand, must be the exact symbol e.g., "5♥", "K♠", "A♦",...)
    "tentative_rule": "Your current best guess about the rule",
    "confidence_level": 0-10,
    "guess_rule": true or false (whether to officially try to guess the rule this turn)
}
</ACTION>

Always provide your current best hypothesis as a tentative rule, even if you're uncertain.
If you set guess_rule to false, this tentative rule will not be evaluated, it's just for your own tracking.
Set "guess_rule" to true only when you want to officially try to guess the rule.
   - If correct, you score and the round ends immediately.
   - If incorrect, you will lose 2 points from your final score, and the round continues.

#### Example:
<ACTION>
{
    "reasoning_summary": "I see red and black cards alternating. My 3♥ is red, last card was black.",
    "card": "3♥",
    "tentative_rule": "Cards must alternate between red and black colors",
    "confidence_level": 8,
    "guess_rule": false
}
</ACTION>

# PATTERN DISCOVERY CARD GAME

You are playing a single-player card game where the goal is to discover a secret rule that determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
This is your turn to play. Your task is to select a card from your hand to play, and optionally try to guess the secret rule.
Your score will depend on how many turns it takes you to correctly identify the rule.
Below you will find the rules of the game, the current game state, your play history, and a description of what you are expected to do.

## RULES OF THE GAME
### Overview
This is a single-player game.
A hidden rule created by the game master determines which cards are accepted or rejected.
Your goal is to play cards and discover the rule as efficiently as possible.

The game uses 2 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards total):
- Ranks: Ace = 1 (low), 2-10, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13. Number cards are 1-10, face cards are 11-13.
- Suits: Hearts ♥️ (red), Diamonds ♦️ (red), Clubs ♣️ (black), Spades ♠️ (black)

The playing area consists of:
- **Mainline:** A horizontal row of accepted cards, ordered left-to-right by time of acceptance
- **Sidelines:** Vertical columns beneath mainline cards. When a card is rejected, it is
  placed in a column below the mainline card it was played after

### Setup

#### Secret Rule

A deterministic secret rule is chosen by the game master.
The rule decides unambiguously whether a newly played card is **accepted** or **rejected**, for every possible card in every possible mainline state.
The rule is simple enough to be described in a single sentence.
The rule depends only on information visible in the mainline: the candidate card and/or any previously accepted mainline cards and their properties (their suits, colors, ranks, parity, positions, etc.)
The rule is deterministic, objective, does not reference sideline rejected cards or hidden information (cards in the deck, cards in your hand...)

Examples of rules:
- The card must be a different color than the last mainline card.
- The card must be a heart or a spade.
- The card must share either the suit or the color with the last mainline card, but not both.
- The card's rank must differ from the last mainline card's rank by exactly 1 or 2.

#### Initial Deal

You start with **12 cards** in your hand.
This hand size remains constant throughout the game, you always draw 1 card after playing.
A starter card that satisfies the rule is placed on the mainline to begin the game.

### Turn Structure

On each turn, you must:
- Play a card from your hand, you then receive feedback (accepted or rejected)
- Optionally try to guess the rule, in order to end the round and score (see below)
- You draw a new card from the deck to maintain your hand size

#### Playing a Card

Once you played a card from your hand to play, you will receive the feedback from the game master, based on the secret rule.
- **If Rejected:** the card goes to a sideline column directly below the last mainline card;
- **If Accepted:** the card becomes the new last mainline card;

### Guessing the Rule

When playing a card, you may attempt to state the rule you believe governs acceptance/rejection.
The game master judges whether your stated rule is **equivalent** to the secret rule.
The wording does not need to match exactly. Only logical equivalence matters.
- **Incorrect guess:** The guess is recorded as wrong and **penalty of 2 points** will later be applied to your final score. Play continues.
- **Correct guess:** The game ends immediately, you score based on the number of turns taken and wrong guesses.

### End Game & Scoring

The game ends when:
1. You **correctly guess the rule**, or
2. You reach the maximum of 30 turns without guessing correctly

Your score is calculated as follows:
Score = (30 - current_turn) - (2 x number_of_failed_guesses)

Score can be negative. **Higher scores are better**. The goal is to discover the rule quickly with few failed guesses.
---


## YOUR TASK: CHOOSE YOUR NEXT ACTION

As a player, this is your turn to play and you must simultaneously:
1. Select a card from your hand to play.
2. Optionally, make a guess about the hidden rule.

### Current game state

Turn: 12 / 30
Penalty so far for 4 wrong guesses: 8
Current potential score if you guess the rule correctly this turn: 11

#### Mainline & Sidelines

This is the mainline and sidelines so far. Rejected cards are shown in brackets after the mainline card they were played after :

A♥ [2♠] [3♣] [8♦] [10♥] [J♥] [9♥] 2♥ 3♦ 4♦ 5♥ 6♥
